page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual CPU mapping and no simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by 32 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio.

Hardware connectivity includes a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps optimized for high-bandwidth internal communication. The instance does not include bundled local storage, relying exclusively on remote EBS storage volumes, and operates without discrete GPU accelerators. Hardware-accelerated cryptographic routines benefit from native AES support, though x86-specific instruction sets like AVX are absent due to the ARM architecture.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier memory subsystem throughput, highlighted by a PassMark memory score in the upper ten percent and uncached 256 MB read bandwidth reaching 298.84 GB/s. Multithreaded computational performance is strong, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,895.0 and elevated PassMark database metrics. Conversely, single-core processing ranks in the middle tier, and large-scale model prompt processing exhibits latency constraints, reflecting the architectural tradeoffs of power-efficient ARM cores compared to high-wattage accelerators.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers high processing density without excessive memory overhead. The instance is suitable for high-throughput network appliances, distributed microservices, batch processing, static web serving, Clang compilation tasks, and moderate-scale in-memory key-value caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated physical cores of 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.8 GHz. Part of the AWS Nitro platform, it provides 32 GB of memory, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio suited for CPU-heavy deployments. The instance includes a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, no local disk storage, and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate superior memory subsystem throughput, with uncached large-block reads achieving 298.84 GB/s and strong multi-core Geekbench metrics. Single-thread execution and LLM prompt processing remain moderate, aligning with the energy-conscious architecture of Graviton processors. Operating without multithreading contention, the server delivers consistent execution profiles for compiled applications, network gateways, containerized microservices, and distributed data processing tasks.
